name: Light Violet-Grey
lede: Light Violet-Grey is a near-neutral medium grey, filed by Ridgway in 1912 under the violet family though its measured chroma is almost zero.

sections.title: A violet with almost no color left
sections.body:
Our naming data files this as a family-word variant of [[light-violet|Light Violet]], the way a modifier like "light" or "dark" extends a base name, rather than from a separate source [1]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas plots it on plate LII at hue 59⁵, and its Munsell notation reads N 5.8, meaning neutral: the recorded chroma is close enough to zero that the "violet" in the name barely survives measurement [1]. In LCH terms it is lightness 59, chroma just 1, hue 226 degrees [1].

Its nearest computed neighbors are, unsurprisingly, named grey: [[grey|Grey]] itself, 2.8 units off, and [[deep-gull-grey|Deep Gull Grey]] and [[traffic-grey-a|Traffic Grey A]], both close [2]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary separately recorded a near match as Puritan Grey in 1912 [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a close match covers enough of the canvas in 468, as photographed (255 by the stricter within-painting measure), which makes it more common than 74 percent of the named colors we track [4]. [[painter:pierre-puvis-de-chavannes|Pierre Puvis de Chavannes]] used it most: it appears in 5 of his 25 works here, 6.6 times the rate of the museums those works come from [4]. On canvas it keeps company with [[dim-grey|Dim Grey]] and [[greyish-black|Greyish Black]] far more than chance, at 16.1 and 11.5 times the expected rate [4].
